evals.prompt: I need a WP-CLI command in my plugin that exports Query Monitor data as JSON. The plugin uses Acme\Blog\ -> src/ PSR-4 autoload. src/Plugin/Main.php has a register() method wiring commands via $this->commandRegistry->add(new \Acme\Blog\CLI\X()). Existing commands in src/CLI/ end with Command suffix (ImportCommand, PurgeCommand). Scaffold the qm-export command following these conventions.
evals.expected_output: A new PHP class under src/CLI/QmExportCommand.php with the project's Command suffix and Acme\Blog\CLI namespace, plus a PHPUnit test stub. Wiring inserted into src/Plugin/Main.php using the project's translated commandRegistry->add() pattern (not the canonical WP_CLI::add_command). No composer require executed.
expectations: The skill picks the wp/cli scaffold (not a guess across multiple candidates).
The skill introspects the project before invoking the engine and reports the four facts: namespace Acme\Blog, base path src, Command suffix, commandRegistry->add() registration pattern.
The engine invocation passes --class=QmExportCommand (project's Command suffix), not the canonical bare QmExport.
The engine invocation passes --namespace=Acme\Blog\CLI (the sub-namespace sampled from the project).
The engine writes the PHP class file and a PHPUnit test stub.
The wiring inserted into src/Plugin/Main.php uses the project's commandRegistry->add() pattern, NOT the canonical WP_CLI::add_command() snippet.
Wiring is shown with an explicit consent prompt before applying.
The skill does NOT run composer require, composer install, or npm install on the user's behalf.

evals.prompt: Set up the GitHub Actions workflow that auto-deploys this WordPress plugin to wordpress.org SVN on each release. The plugin slug is acme-blog. The repo has package.json and composer.json but no .github/workflows directory yet.
evals.expected_output: .github/workflows/cd-wporg.yml written by the engine. The skill surfaces WPORG_USERNAME and WPORG_PASSWORD as a `gh secret set` checklist for the user. No secret values are invented or echoed. No `gh secret set` is executed automatically. actionlint (or yaml-parse) validation result reported.
expectations: The skill picks the ci/cd-wporg scaffold.
The engine invocation passes --plugin-slug=acme-blog.
The engine writes .github/workflows/cd-wporg.yml (and the actionlint test entry references the same file).
Both WPORG_USERNAME and WPORG_PASSWORD are surfaced as a `gh secret set` checklist for the user to run themselves.
The skill does NOT invent secret VALUES (no fake passwords, no 'changeme' placeholders presented as if real).
The skill does NOT execute `gh secret set` itself.
The skill reports the actionlint (or yaml-parse fallback) validation result for the generated YAML.

evals.prompt: Add a dynamic Gutenberg block called pricing-table to my project. Blocks live at src/blocks/ and we use a vendor prefix of 'acme' for block.json names (existing blocks look like acme/hero, acme/cta).
evals.expected_output: src/blocks/pricing-table/ created with block.json (name: acme/pricing-table), edit.js, index.js, render.php. The vendor prefix 'acme' is detected from an existing block.json and applied. No npm install or wp-scripts build executed automatically.
expectations: The skill picks the block/dynamic scaffold.
The skill introspects an existing src/blocks/*/block.json to confirm the 'acme' vendor prefix and the src/blocks/ source directory.
The engine invocation passes a vendor/namespace input that produces 'acme/pricing-table' in the generated block.json (not 'wp-tooling/pricing-table' or unprefixed 'pricing-table').
The engine writes block.json, edit.js, index.js, and render.php under src/blocks/pricing-table/.
The skill does NOT run npm install or wp-scripts build.
